problems.title: Count and share summaries violate necessary covariance identities
problems.source_location: Authors’ arXiv v3, Appendix E.2.6, Tables 5–6, pp. 53–54
claim: Per-seed counts satisfy \(A_r=T_rS_r\), with reported means and standard deviations of counts and shares.
analysis: Cauchy–Schwarz requires \(|\bar A/\bar T-\bar S|\le\sigma_T\sigma_S/\bar T\). Table 5 at FPR \(10^{-3}\) gives \(\bar T=15826,\sigma_T=1239,\bar A=3048,\bar S=0.133,\sigma_S=0.004\). The left side is \(0.05959446\), versus allowed \(0.00031317\); conservative rounding leaves \(0.05905679>0.00035245\). The bound \(T_r\ge\bar T-\sqrt{125}\sigma_T>0\) excludes zero-denominator suppression as an explanation. Table 6 also violates disjoint-bin mean additivity: \(10295+5883=16178\), while the stated union is \(16231\), beyond rounding.
result: Some reported summaries, bin identities or aggregation provenance are incompatible with the definitions. The raw ROC curves and overall AUC are not thereby proved wrong, and the affected entries cannot be identified uniquely.
repair: Regenerate all counts, shares, unions and standard deviations from the same per-seed records with an explicit zero-denominator policy. Do not replace mean shares by ratios of means.
problems.impact_rationale: The contradiction concerns a specific supplementary quantitative decomposition; the broader attack results and instability phenomenon are not independently refuted.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: An infimum plus inclusive threshold is not the conservative rank rule
problems.source_location: Authors’ arXiv v3, Appendix A, p. 17; Appendix E.2.8, p. 57
claim: The paper defines \(\tau=\inf\{t:\widehat F(t^-)\ge1-\eta\}\), uses \(s\ge\tau\), and claims equivalence to a next-distinct order statistic with empirical FPR at most \(\eta\).
analysis: For OUT scores \((1,2,3,4)\) and \(\eta=1/4\), the qualifying set is \((3,\infty)\), whose infimum is \(3\). Inclusive thresholding accepts two scores, giving FPR \(1/2\). The separately supplied next-distinct rule selects \(4\), giving \(1/4\). An infimum need not itself satisfy the left-limit CDF condition. The correct rank instruction is important counterevidence against assuming the experiments used a broken implementation.
result: The formal threshold and claimed equivalence fail, while the intended rank algorithm can preserve empirical calibration. Population FPR is not guaranteed by either finite-set count alone.
repair: Take a minimum over observed scores plus \(+\infty\), or use the empirical quantile with a strict comparison. State the endpoint convention and distinguish new-score decisions between observed levels.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local formal-definition error with a correct alternative already present; actual experimental thresholds are unverified.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Score spacing does not imply inverse-FPR comparison-population size
problems.source_location: Authors’ arXiv v3, Appendix A, Eq. (5), p. 17; Appendix B.2, pp. 19–20
claim: RMIA score spacing \(1/|Z|\) is used to infer a necessary comparison size of inverse minimum FPR.
analysis: Let \(|Z|=2\), both reference ratios be \(1\), comparison constant \(\gamma=1.1\). Of \(1000\) OUT records, give \(999\) ratio \(1\) and one ratio \(2\); give every IN record ratio \(2\). RMIA scores are \(0\) and \(1\). Threshold \(1\) yields FPR \(0.001\), TPR \(1\), despite \(|Z|=2\). An OUT law with masses \(0.999,0.001\) makes both reference draws equal to \(1\) with probability \(0.998001\). Score values and probability mass at those values are different quantities.
result: No distribution-free inverse-FPR requirement follows from quantization alone. Larger comparison sets can still improve the actual measured operating points.
repair: Describe ties and distribution-dependent tail masses; empirical deterministic FPR resolution depends on the OUT calibration sample size and ties.
problems.impact_rationale: The universal necessity rationale fails, without contradicting the measured benefit of more comparison points.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Retraining flip rate alone does not determine positive evidence
problems.source_location: Authors’ arXiv v3, Section 5; Appendix E.2.7, pp. 55–56
claim: The paper distinguishes retraining instability but additionally interprets unstable positive calls as approximately coin-toss evidence.
analysis: Take \(s\mid\mathrm{IN}\sim N(0,1)\), \(s\mid\mathrm{OUT}\sim N(\delta,1)\), \(\delta=\Phi^{-1}(0.99)\), and a likelihood-ratio threshold equivalent to \(s\le0\). Positive probabilities are \(1/2\) under IN and \(0.01\) under OUT. IN retrainings have maximal flip rate \(2(1/2)(1/2)=1/2\), yet a positive event has Bayes factor \(50\). Under prior \(1/2\), posterior membership is \(0.5/(0.5+0.01)=0.980392\). It is unstable repeatability but strong IN-versus-OUT evidence. The paper’s binomial non-rejection label does not itself assert the null is proved.
result: Flip rate measures repeatability, not evidential strength without the competing OUT law and prior. No measured histogram or particular real-record posterior is changed by this countermodel.
repair: Report instability alongside conditional error probabilities or likelihood ratios, and define any stronger reliability claim explicitly.
problems.impact_rationale: The issue limits a conceptual interpretation; the empirical retraining-instability diagnostic remains informative.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

impact_rationale: Minor: specific supplementary summaries and explanatory arguments fail; the core empirical attack comparisons and existence of instability are not shown false.
